content.value_statement: API teams need consistent endpoint docs, examples, and guides. This skill organizes discovery, OpenAPI work, developer guides, examples, interactive docs, and maintenance.
actual_capabilities: Guides endpoint inventory with request, response, authentication, error, and rate-limit details.
Organizes OpenAPI specification creation with paths, schemas, security settings, and examples.
Plans developer guides for onboarding, authentication, usage patterns, troubleshooting, and FAQs.
Structures code example and tutorial work for requests, SDK examples, and curl examples.
Covers interactive documentation setup, documentation site structure, and ongoing maintenance.
Provides quality gates for specifications, guides, examples, interactive docs, and deployment.
limitations: It is a workflow guide and needs API details from the user or project.
It depends on referenced skills that may not be installed in every environment.
It does not validate live endpoints, examples, or deployed documentation automatically.
It does not replace security, legal, or product review of API documentation.

use_cases.title: Document a New API
use_cases.description: Create a complete documentation plan before exposing new endpoints to internal or external users.

use_cases.title: Standardize Existing Docs
use_cases.description: Turn scattered endpoint notes into a consistent OpenAPI spec, guide structure, examples, and quality checklist.

use_cases.title: Plan an API Portal
use_cases.description: Coordinate interactive docs, site navigation, search, tutorials, and maintenance for a developer-facing portal.

prompt_templates.title: Inventory Endpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to inventory my API endpoints. Capture methods, paths, request fields, responses, authentication, errors, and rate limits.

prompt_templates.title: Draft OpenAPI Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to plan an OpenAPI specification. Include paths, schemas, security definitions, examples, and missing information to confirm.

prompt_templates.title: Build Developer Guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to create a developer guide outline. Cover getting started, authentication, common patterns, troubleshooting, FAQs, and examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create Maintenance Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to define API documentation maintenance. Include validation, review steps, update schedules, deployment checks, and feedback monitoring.

output_examples.input: User asks for documentation for a new payment API.
output: Endpoint discovery checklist with authentication, error, and rate-limit fields.
OpenAPI planning outline with required schemas and examples.
Developer guide sections for onboarding, common flows, and troubleshooting.

output_examples.input: User has incomplete API notes across several files.
output: A documentation gap list grouped by endpoint, example, and guide section.
A phased plan for specification cleanup, code examples, and portal updates.

output_examples.input: User wants a public API portal launch checklist.
output: Site structure, navigation, search, and interactive documentation tasks.
Quality gates for tested examples, completed guides, and deployment readiness.

best_practices: Provide current endpoint details, authentication rules, error formats, and rate limits before using the workflow.
Review generated examples against a real staging API before publishing.
Keep OpenAPI specs, guides, examples, and portal content in the same release process.
anti_patterns: Do not publish examples that were not tested against the current API.
Do not omit authentication, rate limits, or error responses from endpoint documentation.
Do not use this workflow when the task is unrelated to API documentation.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps plan API documentation, OpenAPI specs, developer guides, examples, interactive docs, and maintenance steps.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete OpenAPI file by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow and prompts. You still need accurate endpoint details and a generation tool or agent.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs should I prepare first?
faq.answer: Prepare endpoint paths, methods, request fields, response examples, authentication rules, errors, and rate limits.

faq.question: Does it test API examples?
faq.answer: No. It includes testing as a workflow step, but users must run examples against a real API.

faq.question: Is this a security review tool?
faq.answer: No. It can document authentication and errors, but it does not replace security review.
